translation_en: Said ibn Mansur narrated this to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Qanab, from Alqamah ibn Marthad, with this chain. It says: He may take whatever he wishes from his good deeds. The Messenger of Allah turned toward us and said: What do you think?

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us; the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's. They said: Muhammad ibn Jafar narrated to us: Shubah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who heard al-Bara say about the verse, 'Those believers who stay behind are not equal to those who strive in the cause of Allah': The Messenger of Allah ordered Zayd to bring a shoulder blade so he could write it down. Ibn Umm Maktum complained to him about his blindness, and then the verse was revealed: 'Those believers who stay behind, except for those with a disability, are not equal...' (Quran 4:95). Shubah said: Sad ibn Ibrahim also informed me, from a man, from Zayd ibn Thabit, about this verse, with a report like al-Bara's hadith. Ibn Bashshar's narration says: Sad ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from a man, from Zayd ibn Thabit.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Misar, who said: Abu Ishaq narrated to me, from al-Bara, who said: When the verse 'Those believers who stay behind are not equal...' (Quran 4:95) was revealed, Ibn Umm Maktum spoke to the Prophet, and then 'except for those with a disability' was revealed.

Said ibn Amr al-Ashathi and Suwayd ibn Said narrated to us; the wording is Said's. Sufyan informed us, from Amr, who heard Jabir say: A man asked: Messenger of Allah, where will I be if I am killed? He said: In Paradise. The man threw away the dates that were in his hand, then fought until he was killed. Suwayd's narration says that a man asked the Prophet on the day of Uhud.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Zakariyya, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara, who said: A man from Banu al-Nabit came to the Prophet. [Another chain:] Ahmad ibn Janab al-Missisi narrated to us: Isa (Ibn Yunus) narrated to us, from Zakariyya, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara, who said: A man from Banu al-Nabit, a clan of the Ansar, came and said: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that you are His servant and Messenger. Then he advanced and fought until he was killed. The Prophet said: He did little, but was greatly rewarded.

Abu Bakr ibn al-Nadr ibn Abi al-Nadr, Harun ibn Abdullah, Muhammad ibn Rafi, and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us; their wordings are close. They said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us: Sulayman (Ibn al-Mughirah) narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah sent Busaysah as a scout to see what Abu Sufyan's caravan was doing. He came when no one was in the house except me and the Messenger of Allah. I do not know whether he excluded some of his wives. Busaysah told him what had happened. The Messenger of Allah went out and spoke, saying: We have something to pursue. Whoever has his mount at hand, let him ride with us. Some men asked his permission to go get their mounts from the upper part of Madinah. He said: No, only those whose mounts are at hand. The Messenger of Allah and his Companions set out and reached Badr before the polytheists. When the polytheists arrived, the Messenger of Allah said: Let none of you advance toward anything until I am ahead of him. The polytheists drew near, and the Messenger of Allah said: Rise to a Paradise as wide as the heavens and the earth. Umayr ibn al-Humam al-Ansari said: Messenger of Allah, a Paradise as wide as the heavens and the earth? He said: Yes. Umayr said: Wonderful, wonderful! The Messenger of Allah asked: What makes you say 'wonderful, wonderful'? He replied: By Allah, Messenger of Allah, I only hope to be among its people. He said: You are among its people. Umayr took dates from his quiver and began eating them, then said: If I live long enough to eat these dates, that will be a long life. He threw away the dates he had with him, then fought them until he was killed.

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi and Qutaybah ibn Said narrated to us; the wording is Yahya's. Qutaybah said: He narrated to us; Yahya said: Jafar ibn Sulayman informed us, from Abu Imran al-Jawni, from Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Qays, from his father, who said: I heard my father, while facing the enemy, say: The gates of Paradise are beneath the shadows of swords. A man in shabby condition stood up and said: Abu Musa, did you hear the Messenger of Allah say this? He replied: Yes. The man returned to his companions and said: I bid you farewell. Then he broke the sheath of his sword, threw it away, and walked with his sword toward the enemy, striking with it until he was killed.

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Bahz narrated to us: Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, from Thabit, who said: Anas said: My uncle, after whom I was named, did not attend Badr with the Messenger of Allah. He was distressed by this and said: The first battle attended by the Messenger of Allah—I was absent from it. If Allah lets me witness another battle with the Messenger of Allah, Allah will see what I do. He was reluctant to say anything beyond that. He attended Uhud with the Messenger of Allah. Anas said: Sad ibn Muadh came forward, and Anas said to him: Abu Amr, where are you going? He replied: Ah, the scent of Paradise! I find it near Uhud. He fought them until he was killed. More than eighty wounds were found on his body, between blows, stabs, and arrows. His sister, my aunt al-Rubayyi bint al-Nadr, said: I recognized my brother only by his fingertips. This verse was revealed: 'Among the believers are men who have been true to their covenant with Allah; some have fulfilled their vow, and some are still waiting, and they have not changed in the least.' (Quran 33:23) They thought it was revealed concerning him and his companions.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us; the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's. They said: Muhammad ibn Jafar narrated to us: Shubah narrated to us, from Amr ibn Murrah, who said: I heard Abu Wail say: Abu Musa al-Ashari narrated to us that a Bedouin came to the Prophet and said: Messenger of Allah, a man fights for spoils, another fights to be mentioned, and another fights so his position will be seen. Which one is in Allah's cause? The Messenger of Allah said: Whoever fights so that Allah's word is supreme is in Allah's cause.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Numayr, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and Muhammad ibn al-Ala narrated to us. Ishaq said: He informed us; the others said: Abu Muawiyah narrated to us, from al-Amash, from Shaqiq, from Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of Allah was asked about a man who fights out of courage, another who fights out of tribal zeal, and another who fights to show off: Which of these is in Allah's cause? The Messenger of Allah said: Whoever fights so that Allah's word is supreme is in Allah's cause.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us: al-Amash narrated to us, from Shaqiq, from Abu Musa, who said: We came to the Messenger of Allah and said: Messenger of Allah, a man among us fights out of courage... He mentioned a similar report.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: Jarir informed us, from Mansur, from Abu Wail, from Abu Musa al-Ashari, who said: A man asked the Messenger of Allah about fighting in the cause of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. The man said: One fights out of anger and another out of tribal zeal. The Prophet raised his head toward him—and he raised his head only because he had been standing—and said: Whoever fights so that Allah's word is supreme is in Allah's cause.

Yahya ibn Habib al-Harithi narrated to us: Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us: Yunus ibn Yusuf narrated to me, from Sulayman ibn Yasar, who said: The people dispersed from around Abu Hurayrah, and the Syrian notable Natil said to him: Sheikh, narrate to us a hadith you heard from the Messenger of Allah. He said: Yes. I heard the Messenger of Allah say: The first person to be judged on the Day of Resurrection will be a man who was martyred. He will be brought, and Allah will make him recognize His blessings, and he will recognize them. Allah will ask: What did you do with them? He will say: I fought for You until I was martyred. Allah will say: You have lied. You fought so that it would be said, 'He is brave,' and it was said. Then He will order that he be dragged on his face until he is cast into the Fire. Then a man who learned knowledge, taught it, and recited the Quran will be brought. Allah will make him recognize His blessings, and he will recognize them. Allah will ask: What did you do with them? He will say: I learned and taught knowledge and recited the Quran for Your sake. Allah will say: You have lied. You learned so that it would be said, 'He is a scholar,' and you recited the Quran so that it would be said, 'He is a reciter,' and it was said. Then He will order that he be dragged on his face until he is cast into the Fire. Then a man to whom Allah gave abundant wealth from every kind of property will be brought. Allah will make him recognize His blessings, and he will recognize them. Allah will ask: What did you do with them? He will say: I left no way in which You love wealth to be spent without spending it for Your sake. Allah will say: You have lied. You did it so that it would be said, 'He is generous,' and it was said. Then He will order that he be dragged on his face and cast into the Fire.

Ali ibn Khashram informed us: al-Hajjaj (Ibn Muhammad) informed us, from Ibn Jurayj: Yunus ibn Yusuf narrated to me, from Sulayman ibn Yasar, who said: The people dispersed from around Abu Hurayrah, and Natil of Syria asked him. He related the hadith in a manner like Khalid ibn al-Harith's narration.

Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Abdullah ibn Yazid Abu Abd al-Rahman narrated to us: Haywah ibn Shurayh narrated to us, from Abu Hani, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli, from Abdullah ibn Amr, that the Messenger of Allah said: Whenever a raiding party goes out in Allah's cause and obtains spoils, they have received two-thirds of their reward early, while one-third remains for them in the Hereafter. If they obtain no spoils, their full reward remains for them.

Muhammad ibn Sahl al-Tamimi narrated to me: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us: Nafi ibn Yazid informed us: Abu Hani narrated to me: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli narrated to me, from Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: No raiding party or detachment goes out and gains spoils and returns safely except that they have received two-thirds of their reward early. No raiding party or detachment fails and suffers losses except that their full reward is given.

Abdullah ibn Maslamah ibn Qanab narrated to us: Malik narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Said, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Alqamah ibn Waqqas, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: Actions are only by intentions, and each person will have only what he intended. Whoever's migration was to Allah and His Messenger, his migration was to Allah and His Messenger. Whoever's migration was for some worldly gain or a woman to marry, his migration is to what he migrated for.

Muhammad ibn Rumh ibn al-Muhajir informed us: al-Layth informed us. [Another chain:] Abu al-Rabi al-Ataki narrated to us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us. [Another chain:] Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Abd al-Wahhab (al-Thaqafi) narrated to us. [Another chain:] Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar Sulayman ibn Hayyan narrated to us. [Another chain:] Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us: Hafs (Ibn Ghiyath) and Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us. [Another chain:] Muhammad ibn al-Ala al-Hamdani narrated to us: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us. [Another chain:] Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us. All report from Yahya ibn Said with Malik's chain and the meaning of his hadith. Sufyan's narration says: I heard Umar ibn al-Khattab inform people from the pulpit about the Prophet.

Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us: Thabit narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: Whoever sincerely asks for martyrdom will be granted it, even if martyrdom does not befall him.

Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me; the wording is Harmalah's. Abu al-Tahir said: He informed us; Harmalah said: Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us: Abu Shurayh narrated to me, that Sahl ibn Abi Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf narrated to him, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Prophet said: Whoever sincerely asks Allah for martyrdom, Allah will bring him to the stations of the martyrs, even if he dies in his bed. Abu al-Tahir did not mention 'sincerely' in his narration.

Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Sahm al-Antaki informed us: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Wuhayb al-Makki, from Umar ibn Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Sumayy, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: Whoever dies without having fought and without having even thought of doing so has died with a branch of hypocrisy. Ibn Sahm said: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: We think this applied during the time of the Messenger of Allah.

Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from al-Amash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: We were with the Prophet on an expedition, and he said: There are men in Madinah who were with you on every journey you made and every valley you crossed; illness kept them behind.

Yahya ibn Yahya informed us: Abu Muawiyah informed us. [Another chain:] Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Said al-Ashajj said: Waki narrated to us. [Another chain:] Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: Isa ibn Yunus informed us. All report from al-Amash with this chain, except that Waki's narration says: 'They shared in your reward.'

Yahya ibn Yahya said: I read to Malik, from Ishaq ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah used to visit Umm Haram bint Milhan, and she would feed him. Umm Haram was married to Ubadah ibn al-Samit. One day the Messenger of Allah came to her, and she fed him. Then she sat and picked through his hair. The Messenger of Allah slept, then woke up laughing. She asked: What makes you laugh, Messenger of Allah? He said: Some people from my community were shown to me as fighters in Allah's cause, sailing on the back of this sea like kings on thrones—or like kings on thrones. The narrator was uncertain which of the two he said. She said: Messenger of Allah, ask Allah to make me one of them. He prayed for her, then laid his head down and slept. He awoke laughing again. She asked: What makes you laugh, Messenger of Allah? He said: Some people from my community were shown to me as fighters in Allah's cause, as he had said before. She said: Messenger of Allah, ask Allah to make me one of them. He said: You are among the first. Umm Haram bint Milhan sailed on the sea during Muawiyah's time. When she came out of the sea, she fell from her mount and died.

Khalaf ibn Hisham narrated to us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Said, from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban, from Anas ibn Malik, from Umm Haram, Anas's maternal aunt, who said: One day the Prophet came to us and stayed with us. He awoke laughing. I asked: What makes you laugh, Messenger of Allah? May my father and mother be sacrificed for you. He said: I was shown people from my community sailing on the sea like kings on thrones. I said: Ask Allah to make me one of them. He said: You are one of them. She said: Then he slept and awoke again laughing. I asked him, and he said the same as before. I said: Ask Allah to make me one of them. He said: You are among the first. Later Ubadah ibn al-Samit married her and went on a sea expedition, taking her with him. When she came ashore, a mule was brought near for her to ride. It threw her, and her neck was broken.

Muhammad ibn Rumh ibn al-Muhajir and Yahya ibn Yahya informed us: al-Layth informed us, from Yahya ibn Said, from Ibn Habban, from Anas ibn Malik, from his maternal aunt Umm Haram bint Milhan, who said: One day the Messenger of Allah slept near me, then awoke smiling. She said: Messenger of Allah, what made you smile? He said: People from my community were shown to me sailing on the back of this green sea. Then he mentioned a report like Hammad ibn Zayd's hadith.

Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr narrated to me. They said: Ismail (Ibn Jafar) narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, who heard Anas ibn Malik say: The Messenger of Allah came to Milhan's daughter, Anas's maternal aunt, and rested his head beside her. He related the hadith with the meaning of Ishaq ibn Abi Talhah and Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban's reports.

Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Bahram al-Darimi narrated to us: Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to us: Layth (Ibn Sad) narrated to us, from Ayyub ibn Musa, from Makhul, from Shurahbil ibn al-Simt, from Salman, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah say: Guarding the frontier for a day and a night is better than fasting for a month and praying during its nights. If he dies, the deeds he used to do continue to be recorded for him, his provision continues to be given to him, and he is protected from the tester.

Abu al-Tahir informed me: Ibn Wahb informed us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Shurayh, from Abd al-Karim ibn al-Harith, from Abu Ubaydah ibn Utbah, from Shurahbil ibn al-Simt, from Salman al-Khayr, from the Messenger of Allah, with the meaning of Layth's hadith from Ayyub ibn Musa.

Yahya ibn Yahya said: I read to Malik, from Sumayy, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said: While a man was walking along a road, he found a thorny branch on the road and moved it aside. Allah appreciated this for him and forgave him. He also said: There are five kinds of martyrs: one who dies of plague, one who dies of a stomach illness, one who drowns, one who dies beneath a collapsed structure, and one who is martyred in the cause of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
